cues.say: Every dashboard, every filter, every report asks the same question.
On five million rows, a B tree counts the matches one at a time.
Gin has to go back and read the table.
cues.cap: GIN has to go back and read the table.

cues.say: Meet Lion. A roaring bitmap index for Postgress.
Lion keeps each value's rows as compressed bitmaps, in chunks that know their own counts.
So it adds up chunks, instead of walking rows.
The same count: one point seven milliseconds. Ninety times faster than a B tree.
cues.cap: The same count: 1.7 milliseconds. 90× faster than a B-tree.

cues.say: Two filters: nine times faster. GROUP BY: twenty-four times. Array tags: a hundred and sixty-eight times faster than gin.
cues.cap: Two filters: 9× faster. GROUP BY: 24×. Array tags: 168× faster than GIN.

cues.say: And it's just an index. Create it, vacuum, and Postgress uses it for the count queries you already write.
cues.cap: And it's just an index. Create it, VACUUM, and Postgres uses it for the count queries you already write.

cues.say: Keep your B trees for lookups and ordering, and gin for text search. Add Lion where you count.
P G Lion. Try it on your data.
